title: Chocolate Swiss Roll (Bûche de Noël)
summary: A light chocolate Swiss roll filled with vanilla cream and covered in chocolate ganache bark, shaped into the traditional Yule log for the festive table.
equipment: 23 x 33 cm Swiss roll tin, lined with baking paper
stand mixer or electric hand whisk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt, or table salt
dark chocolate (about 60% cocoa solids), finely chopped

steps.title: Whisk the eggs to a foam
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) for at least 20 minutes and line the Swiss roll tin with baking paper. Whisk the eggs, sugar and salt on high speed for 6-8 minutes until the mixture has roughly tripled in volume and holds a ribbon trail for about 5 seconds when the whisk is lifted. There's no other raising agent in this sponge, so all of its lift comes from the air beaten in at this stage.

steps.title: Fold in flour and cocoa
steps.text: Sift the flour and cocoa powder over the whisked eggs in two additions, folding each in gently with a large metal spoon rather than stirring. Spread the batter evenly out to the corners of the tin with a palette knife. Gentle folding keeps the air bubbles intact, which is what gives the baked sponge enough flexibility to roll without tearing.

steps.title: Bake and roll while hot
steps.text: Bake for 8-10 minutes until the sponge feels just springy; a minute or two too long and it dries out and cracks when rolled. Turn the sponge out immediately onto a sheet of baking paper dusted with sugar, peel away the lining paper, then roll it up from a short end with the fresh paper inside and wrap it in a tea towel to cool completely. Rolling it while still warm trains the sponge into a curl, so it won't crack later when it's unrolled for filling.

steps.title: Make the ganache bark
steps.text: Bring the cream and golden syrup to the boil, pour it over the chopped chocolate, leave for 2 minutes, then stir until smooth and glossy. Leave the ganache at room temperature for 1-1½ hours until it thickens to a spreadable consistency. The syrup keeps the set slightly soft, which is what lets it spread thinly like bark instead of setting hard.

steps.title: Fill and re-roll the sponge
steps.text: Whip the double cream with the icing sugar and vanilla to soft-firm peaks. Unroll the cooled sponge, spread the cream over it evenly, leaving a 2 cm bare strip at the far end, then roll it back up without the paper, finishing with the seam underneath. That bare strip stops cream from squeezing out of the end as the roll tightens. Chill the filled log for 30 minutes to firm up.

steps.title: Shape and bark the log
steps.text: Slice a 6 cm piece off one end of the log at an angle and set it against the side of the log to look like a branch. Cover the whole log and branch with the ganache using a palette knife. Drag a fork lengthways along the ganache to score ridges that look like bark. Chill for 1 hour until firm, then dust with icing sugar just before serving.

tips: Don't overbake the sponge - a few minutes past springy and it turns too dry and brittle to roll without cracking.
Roll the warm sponge with paper inside straight after baking; skipping this step is the main reason rolled sponges crack later.
Let the ganache cool to a spreadable, not pourable, consistency before using it as bark, or it will slide straight off the log.
Leave a bare border when spreading the cream filling so it doesn't squeeze out of the ends as you re-roll.
Chill the finished log before slicing so the ganache and filling hold their shape.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep the log covered in the fridge and eat within 3 days; it's not suitable for freezing once filled with whipped cream. Serve chilled, straight from the fridge.
